ci(agentic-docs): pass the Actions run URL to the job (#4364)

The bot now comments on an issue when a run starts, so whoever labelled it can
see that something is happening rather than waiting 15-25 minutes with no sign.
That comment links the run, which means the job has to be told where the run is:
RUN_URL, assembled here from github.run_id.

Nothing attacker-controlled is added to the boundary — the URL is built from the
run's own id, not from anything a commenter wrote, and an Actions run URL
contains no comma, so it is safe in the comma-separated --update-env-vars list.
Without it the job simply omits the link.

Also corrects three comments that still described the older behaviour where a
/position comment on an issue started a run. The `if:` condition itself is
unchanged: only a labelled issue, or a comment or review on one of the bot's own
pull requests, triggers anything.

read the tool calls a spoken block runs into, and report the checks the pass rate leaves out (#98)

* read the tool calls a spoken block runs into, and report the checks the pass rate leaves out

The launcher prints `says`, its indented text, then that turn's tool calls, with
nothing between them. The parser appended every indented line to the spoken block
and swallowed the calls, so a run whose trace records 11 tools parsed as zero and
the 18 checks that read the transcript all reported `N/A`.

A line now closes the spoken block as soon as it carries another event. Inside a
block the shape alone decides nothing, because prose is indented the same way, so
a call has to be named in the run trace or carry a server or a JSON argument.
`build_context` passes the trace's tool names down for that.

`pass_rate` still divides by TRUE plus FALSE. `decided_count` and `na_count` are
reported beside it and the tally goes into `summary`, so a rate over a third of
the checks no longer reads like a rate over all of them.

Closes dlt-hub/dlthub-ai-workbench-internal#83

* pin the parser against the transcript of the run that reported the bug

The 11 tool calls of a real deployed inspector run, checked in as a fixture with
the ids and the workspace name replaced. The pre-fix parser reads 0 calls out of
it and 11 of the new tests fail; the fixed one reads all 11 in order, with their
arguments and servers.

`test_prepare_scores_what_a_deployed_run_did` runs the whole preparation over it:
12 of the 18 transcript checks decide, the other 6 state a condition that did not
apply. Every one of the 18 was `N/A` before.

* commit the transcript fixture the tests read

`*.log` in .gitignore dropped it. The suite passed locally because the file was
on disk, and CI could not read it at all: five tests failed with FileNotFoundError.

Negate the rule for `tests/**/fixtures/**` rather than renaming the file, so the
next captured log a test needs does not go the same way.

* let the judge run on any provider the loop reaches

The evaluator named no provider in its definition, but the README pinned
`model="sonnet"` in the deployment snippet and its model table had no Azure row,
so a workspace whose key opens an Azure endpoint could not copy either.

Drop the pin, document `agent.model`, `agent.api_key`, `agent.api_url` and
`agent.api_version` as one set, and say which of the four Azure needs. Note that
`loop: claude-agent-sdk` takes Anthropic models only, which is the one way to
make the evaluator provider-specific.

Raise `max_tokens` to 1,000,000, matching the inspector. A platform run used
658,952 against a judge input of about 6,000 tokens and died on the 600,000
limit with nothing to report: 25 turns cost more than that ceiling allows.

Record that what the transcript holds depends on the model, not only on the loop.

* raise on the abort path instead of returning

`_invoke_agent` sends any returned dict carrying `status` into `_finish`, which
reads `loop.trace`. On the abort path the loop never ran, so returning
`prep.aborted_output` failed the run with `AgentTraceNotAvailable` and lost the
reason the evaluator aborted. Raising skips `_finish`.

Workaround for dlt-hub/dlthub-ai-workbench-internal#84. Drop it once dlt tolerates
a loop that never ran.

* keep a sentence quoting a tool error from ending a spoken block

`_TOOL_ERROR_LINE` matches anywhere on the line, so an agent narrating "the first
attempt hit Error calling tool 'x'" cut its own spoken block short and invented a
tool_error event.

The launcher logs a tool error at column 0, or under the logger's own indent when
it repeats a timestamp. Neither is the two spaces that mark spoken text, so that
is what tells the two apart. Both logged forms appear on real runs and both still
read as errors.

add job-inspector-eval, an evaluation agent for job-inspector (#95)

* add job-inspector-eval, an evaluation agent for job-inspector

Every instruction in the job-inspector body maps to one check. 57 of them: 34
computed in Python, 1 hybrid, 22 answered by a judge. Each returns TRUE, FALSE
or N/A with a reasoning, and N/A is a legitimate answer that names its
condition.

checks.py computes what can be computed from data and extracts the bounded
evidence the judge reads, so the judge never sees a whole log. finalize writes
the computed results over the judge's output, so the model cannot alter them.
The agent is deployed as a function driving the installed definition, which is
what gives the deterministic layer a place to run before and after the loop.

Also moves the agents folder from dlthub/agents/ to agents/, which is the path
`dlthub ai toolkit install` reads. Neither agent installed before this.

Verified end to end on a dev workspace: a failing pipeline triggers the
inspector, the inspector triggers the evaluator, and the evaluation is stored
against the inspector run. The deterministic checks are covered by unit tests
with hand-written fixtures, several of them taken from real runs that produced
wrong outcomes.

* hold the comments in checks.py to one line each

* fail the eval on an unanswered check and on a wrong line citation

An open check the judge left unanswered was reported `N/A` while the evaluation stayed
`succeeded` and could still report `passed`. An empty or truncated judge response read as
a clean inspector run. An evaluation that lost checks now fails and never passes, which
covers a check that raised too.

An excerpt found in the log but not at the line cited passed `evidence_excerpts_exist`
with a note. `evidence_cited_at_line` now fails it, and `earliest_error_window` anchors on
the line the excerpt sits on, so a citation pointing too early no longer hides the errors
before the real line.

* address the review on job-inspector-eval: narrower write detection, no anchor on an unplaced excerpt, a blind parser fails the run

* hold the transcript checks at N/A when the parser read no tool call

give job-inspector a stopping rule for credential checks and a budget rule (#94)

* give job-inspector a stopping rule for credential checks and a budget rule

The inspector spent its whole turn budget widening a credential check and
hit the request limit before writing any output, so the failure it had
already diagnosed was never reported.

Add a Budget section: the earliest error naming a cause ends the
investigation, going past it needs an alternative you name first, a call
that returns nothing has answered, search stays inside the workspace, and
a run short of turns writes what it has.

Add a Checking credentials section naming the one pass that constitutes a
check, with nothing configured as the finding rather than a reason to keep
looking. Wire the secrets and config tool groups so secrets_view_redacted
and dlthub_list_variables are actually available; both add only read tools
the agent's access already covers.

Name the re-run commands in the read-only constraint and rule out reading
secrets files directly, the two escalations the same runaway produced.

Closes #80

* make the credential pass mandatory and fix two output fields

The same instruction failed in both directions: with the default budget an
unbounded search, and with a nudge to finish the check skipped entirely. A
stopping rule alone produces the second failure.

Require the credential pass before classifying `credentials` or proposing
that a secret be set or rotated, and carve it out of the budget rule so a
run told to report early still makes the two calls. Say that an entry which
exists proves the credential is configured, not valid, and cap confidence
at medium in that case.

Ask for the line number in `evidence.source` rather than showing one in an
example, and tell the agent to fill `proposed_fix` even when `summary`
already spells the remedy out.

* make rung 4 of the run resolution terminal

With no run id, no job ref and a manual trigger, the inspector listed every
run in the workspace, picked two itself and read eleven logs, burning
1,021,153 tokens without producing output. Rung 4 was a bullet in the same
register as the three above it, so nothing marked it as the end of the
procedure.

Cut the list to three rungs and put the abort in its own paragraph after
them: running out of rungs stops the inspection, and listing runs, picking
one or reading a log are all out. Add to "One run at a time" that listing
runs serves the neighbour check of a run you were given, never the search
for one to inspect.

* bound the credential pass to the unified view and survive a tool error

A keyed pydantic-ai run showed the default-budget scenario still running
away, and failing in a way the previous commit introduced: the agent walked
`secrets_view_redacted` file by file with `path=`, two absent files raised,
and `retries: 1` ended the run at turn 54 with no output.

Say the check is `secrets_view_redacted` with no arguments, since the
unified view already merges every file, and `dlthub_list_variables` once for
the run's profile. Treat a tool error as an answer alongside an empty
result. Forbid reading another run's log, which the same run did for
`a400ef95`. Raise `retries` to 2 so one tool error cannot cost a diagnosis
the agent already has.

* take the shell off job-inspector so secrets are unreachable, not forbidden

An instruction not to `cat` a secrets file is not a control. dlt's deny
rules cover the file tools only: Read, Glob and Grep refuse `*secrets.toml`
and `.env`, while `local: execute` hands over Bash and RunPython, which
nothing filters. A keyed run bore that out, running `cat .dlt/prod.secrets.toml`
one turn after being told not to.

Drop `execute`. The inspection needs the MCP tools and the file tools, and
without a shell there is no `cat`, no `grep`, no Python that opens a secrets
file, and no way to re-run the job under inspection.

Cut the prose the shell required: the command block, the CLI fallbacks, the
`cat`/`grep` prohibitions and the re-run list. Trim "Checking credentials"
to the two calls and what an empty result means. Body drops from 166 lines
to 148.

* cut the redundant lines from the credentials and budget sections

* make the trace read conditional and stop on a tool error that retrying cannot fix

feat(cli): hand off onboarding to your coding agent (#60)

# Overview

Reworks the `dlthub-start` onboarding so the CLI sets the workspace up and then **hands off to your coding agent**, instead of running the sample pipeline and opening the dashboard itself. Also tightens the setup output and copy so the run reads cleanly.

## Changes

**Flow (`cli.py`)**
- After scaffolding, installing deps, logging in, and connecting a `playground` workspace, the CLI hands off to the chosen agent rather than running `load_sample_shop` / opening the dashboard.
- Agent selection and launching are now separate steps: pick an agent, then choose to launch it (it deploys and runs the sample pipeline via the `deploy-run-sample-pipeline` skill) or skip and get the prompt printed + copied to paste into an agent yourself.
- On login / playground-connection failure the CLI **still hands off** — with a prompt asking the agent to help resolve the error (deps are installed, so the `dlthub` CLI works). `uv sync` failure still exits with the error (no CLI = no hand-off).
- Collapsed scaffold + `uv sync` into one step and login + playground connection into another; login runs quietly (output surfaces only on error).

**Copy (`strings.py`)**
- One canonical hand-off prompt (launched / pasted / non-TTY) embedding the skill's absolute path so the agent finds it from any cwd; the launch-plan preview shows a short workspace-relative path.
- Launch plan states what will happen ("let {agent} deploy and run…" / "Setup hit an error — let {agent} help resolve it…"), self-documenting launch choices, and an outcome-matched closing panel ("You're all set" / "Almost there").
- Removed stale "build dlt pipelines / first run / open the dashboard" wording and an orphaned string.

**Other modules**
- `display.py`: `print_next_steps` takes `agent_prompt` + `panel_title`.
- `prompts.py`: `confirm()` supports custom yes/no labels.
- `config.py`: added `AGENT_SKILLS_DIR` (drift-checked against the scaffold); bumped `WORKBENCH_REF`.

**Docs**
- Updated README, CONTRIBUTING, the scaffold README, the `workspace-here` Makefile help, the `pyproject` description, and the CHANGELOG to match the new flow; fixed stale `--yes`/`--skip-uv-sync` references (now `--setup-only`/`--scaffold-only`) and the codex `.agents/` directory.

**Bundled workbench**
- Regenerated `_agents/**` from the bumped `WORKBENCH_REF`: the `toolkit-dispatch` skill is now `dlthub-router`, which routes to and installs the right workflow toolkit on demand. Refreshed the scaffold `uv.lock` (`dlt` 1.28.1).

## Tests

- New/updated unit tests across `test_cli.py`, `test_display.py`, `test_config.py`, `test_prompts.py` covering the hand-off paths (launch / decline / unlaunchable agent / non-TTY / login-failure resolve), the outcome panel titles, the quiet login, and the `AGENT_SKILLS_DIR` mapping.
- `133 passed`; `ruff` and `mypy` clean.
- Smoke-tested `make workspace-local` end-to-end (scaffold → quiet login/connect → hand-off).

- **docs**: document the dev/local targets, flags, and `version-upgrade` in CONTRIBUTING; fix the `make publish` command.

## Tests

chore(scaffold): sync workspace deps with dlt WORKSPACE_DEPS and check for drift (#25)

* Add workspace deps sync and drift check

The bundled scaffold's dependency list is a copy of dlt's WORKSPACE_DEPS,
which upstream documents as kept in sync but nothing enforced. The copy sat
frozen at dlt's 2026-05-10 state and drifted.

scripts/sync_workspace_deps.py reads WORKSPACE_DEPS from the dlt wheel the
scaffold's uv.lock resolves, so the lock stays the only pin. It parses the
wheel rather than importing dlt, since dlthub-init deliberately does not
depend on dlt. 'make scaffold-deps-sync' rewrites the list, and
'make scaffold-deps-check' fails on drift in CI and 'make ci'.

BASE_SPECS (dlt[hub], dlthub, dlthub-client) is this repo's own prefix and is
never rewritten by a sync; trimming those is a separate decision.

* Sync scaffold deps with dlt 1.30.0 WORKSPACE_DEPS

Applies the first sync: adds s3fs>=2022.4.0 (dlt-hub/dlt#4044) and drops the
python_version >= '3.10' markers on ibis-framework and fastmcp, which upstream
removed with Python 3.9 support (dlt-hub/dlt#4074). Re-resolves the bundled
uv.lock.

s3fs pulls aiobotocore/aiohttp/botocore, taking a synced workspace from 415 MB
/ 120 packages to 444 MB / 133. Upstream carries it so the job and module
launchers can prune it from their runtime requirements and get it pinned from
the workspace lock instead of installing it unpinned at deploy time.

Run check-skills in CI (#26)

'make check-skills' was only reachable via 'make ci' locally, so skills/
drifting from the pinned workbench ref would not fail a pull request. Adds a
skills-check job mirroring lock-check.

Placed above lock-check rather than as another step in it, so this does not
collide with the workspace deps drift check landing in a separate PR.

fix(cli): install venv in non-interactive terminals instead of crashing (#11)

* fix(cli): install venv in non-interactive terminals instead of crashing

When stdin is not a TTY (piped input, CI, coding agents) and neither
--yes nor --no-sync is passed, the venv/uv confirmation prompts called
beaupy.select, which raises `termios.error: (25, 'Inappropriate ioctl
for device')`. That error fell through to the generic handler and the
run failed with "Unexpected error" and exit code 1, leaving no venv.

confirm() now detects a non-interactive stdin and returns the prompt's
default (Yes) instead of invoking beaupy, so a non-TTY run installs uv
if missing and runs `uv sync` unattended. --yes and --no-sync behavior
is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(cli): point non-interactive next steps at bundled skills

In a non-TTY run the final "Next steps" line now tells the agent to use
the bundled skills in .agents/skills/ instead of "open your coding agent
and tell it what to build", which assumes a human at an interactive
terminal. Interactive runs are unchanged.
